**LiFePO4 is the better choice for most people.** It lasts several times longer, and it fails less violently. NMC's main advantage is energy per pound, but that gap is smaller in finished power stations than in the cells.

**Why LiFePO4 usually wins**

- **Cycle life:** The models compared in [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) are rated for 3,000 cycles to 80%, versus 500 for the NMC model. [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/) reports a median of 4,000 cycles for LFP models and 800 for NMC. Daily users would reach the NMC rating in a couple of years. Occasional users may never reach it, but batteries also age with time.
- **Safety:** In the 2020 study cited by UnpluggedWatts, LFP cells released smoke without flames when they failed, while every NMC cell ignited. OutageMath cites two lab studies (Lei et al., 2017; Golubkov et al., 2015) showing LFP cells peaked at much lower temperatures than NMC or NCA. These are small cells, though, so treat the direction as more reliable than the exact numbers.
- **Price:** The median price per Wh is $0.55 for LiFePO4 and $0.95 for NMC, per [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc). Most mainstream brands now use LiFePO4.

**Where NMC still makes sense**

- **Weight:** NMC stores more energy per pound. The finished-unit gap is modest: about 10% in OutageMath's database and about 16% in powerstations.reviews' table. It matters most for units you carry.
- **Light use:** A few uses per year means cycle life is less of a constraint.
- **Existing units:** If you already own a working NMC station, keep using it.

The sources give different NMC cycle figures (500 to 2,000) and thermal-runaway temperatures, so I'd rely on the cycle rating printed on the specific model you're considering.
